items.title: Failure of base change in degree q produces a field-valued counterexample
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file etale-cohomology.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma upgrades a failure of base change in degree q to a counterexample over the spectrum of a field: assuming BC(f, n, q-1) holds but BC(f, n, q) does not, it produces a commutative diagram with T = Spec(K) and a sheaf on Spec(K) annihilated by n for which the base change map in degree q is not an isomorphism (statement lines 17078-17094, with the standing notation delivered as a context span from lines 16847-16866). The proof is an application of the same-chapter formal argument lemma, and its content is the verification of the three hypotheses for the property P that a scheme over T still carries a counterexample: thickening-invariance follows from topological invariance of the etale site (proof lines 17161-17164), limit-stability from the behaviour of pullbacks and cohomology under limits (proof lines 17167-17201), and the decomposition condition, which the author calls the most interesting, is proved by restricting the counterexample to a closed subscheme or to its quasi-compact complement (proof lines 17204-17293). The non-formal content is concentrated in that last verification. The claim is H2: a long but fully written-out verification, assembled by an explicitly cited formal principle.
